In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the normal scheme of the geographic or orogenetic cycle is the one which best fits the general conditions of the present time.

the geographic cycle, in its normal form, is a sequence of events which begins with the emergence of the land surface from the sea and ends with the final lowering and levelling of the land surface by stream action.

the normal scheme of the geographic (or physiographic) cycle is the one most commonly met with in the humid temperate zone, and that in the arid zone it is modified by the addition of an initial phase of deflation, and that in a glacial climate it is modified by an added phase of glacial erosion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the normal scheme of the geographic or denudation cycle, as developed by Davis, has to be modified for the conditions of an arid climate in the direction of greater emphasis on the role of wind in the work of erosion and of transportation, and in the direction of less emphasis on the role and power of water.

we have shown that the geographic cycle, as developed in a humid climate, is modified in a glacial climate by the presence of the ice sheet and the ice cap; that the cycle, as developed for a humid climate, may be modified in an arid region by the action of wind and sand.
the deflative scheme of erosion is a process of regional lowering by which an arid climate tends to produce a surface of gentle relief.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geographic cycle is a process that is not linear.
the geographic cycle in a humid climate has been the dominant factor in the shaping of the earth’s surface.
the geographic cycle is not just about the physical processes of land formation, but also about the cultural and social processes that shape the landscape.
